sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier: head in dorsal view usually nearly black on the anterior 2/3, rusty to dark chestnut brown posteriorly, with a pair of very pale orange-yellow spots at the extreme posterior end; the genal lower margin with a characteristic pale orange-yellow rim. Frontal margin rounded in cross-section, its outline nearly circular in frontal view; frontal face meeting the vertex face at 70—80°; frontal horns rounded and stout, especially broad in lateral view, projecting anterolaterally, discontinuous with the frontal margin in dorsal view and separated from the clypeus by a deep groove; mandibles very short, angled, the apex not extending beyond the lateral margin of the labrum when closed; compound eyes absent or reduced to small slits. Alate: body pale yellow-brown, almost uniform; head oval and elongate; antennae 16—18-segmented, mostly 17, segment formula 2>3=4=5. Closest to C. parvifrons, but distinctly larger.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Body pale yellow-brown, nearly monochrome. Sclerotized veins yellow-brown, the wing membrane nearly transparent. Chevron mark of the wing scale very faint. Frontal face, labrum, pronotum and sternites pale yellow-brown; vertex, antennae and abdominal tergites yellow-brown. Femora yellowish white, the legs including the ends of the tibiae pale yellow-brown. Head oval and elongate, the cranial sutures distinct, often masked by the pale background. Compound eyes medium-sized, oval, with a straight edge only along the antennal socket. Ocelli rather small, oval, touching the compound eyes. Antennae 16—18-segmented, mostly 17, the segment formula variable, often 2>3=4=5. Pronotum usually distinctly wider than the head width (including the compound eyes), occasionally equal; anterior margin moderately concave, the sides slightly convex, posterior margin weakly concave; midline and transverse band of the pronotum almost absent. Subcosta of the forewing long, reaching 1/4 of the wing length from the wing base; radial vein reaching near the middle of the wing; radial sector with 5—7 branches. Arolia present.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head pigmentation variable in dorsal view, usually nearly black on the anterior 2/3, occasionally only on the anterior 1/3; the posterior part rusty, chestnut brown or dark chestnut brown; the extreme posterior end with a pair of small, very pale orange-yellow spots. In lateral view the anterior 1/2 of the head almost black, the posterior half variable, usually tinged chestnut brown, and with a characteristic, distinctly paler orange-yellow genal lower margin. Mandibles chestnut brown. Anterior margin of the pronotum rusty orange, the remainder pale yellow. Head outline in dorsal view variable: in some specimens the sides parallel, in others swollen behind a constriction at the anterior 1/5. Anterior outline of the head in dorsal view shallowly concave, with another small concavity at the middle. Middle of the vertex with a shallow concavity. Vertex outline in lateral view with a distinct concavity, accentuated by the swelling of the posterior part of the vertex. Sculpture shallow but dense, covering most of the head capsule surface (including the frontal margin and the frontal face), smooth only in the median area of the frontal face. Frontal margin distinct, rounded in cross-section; often directly continuous with the vertex; in some individuals slightly delimited from the vertex at the middle; outline nearly circular in frontal view. Frontal face meeting the vertex face at 70—80°. Labrum short, broadly rounded, swollen at the apex, the apical setae short. Frontal horns rounded and stout, especially broad in lateral view, projecting outward and downward; discontinuous with the frontal margin in dorsal view, with a deep groove between them and the clypeus. Genal horns small rounded projections adjacent to the frontal horns. Mandibles very short, angled, slightly swollen at the base in some specimens; upturned in lateral view; the apex not extending beyond the lateral margin of the labrum when closed; dentition weak. Compound eyes absent, or small and slit-like; large and oval in soldier-nymph intermediates. Antennae 11—14-segmented, mostly 12 or 14; segment formula mostly 2>3>4=5. Anterior margin of the pronotum very shallowly notched, the sides almost parallel or narrowed posteriorly over the anterior half, the posterior half broadly rounded; anterior margin weakly undulate, posterior margin straight. Comparison with C. parvifrons: in the latter the median notch of the frontal margin bears zipper-like alternating corrugations, whereas in the present species the notch is weak or absent and lacks corrugations; the present species has shorter mandibles.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Type locality: 4 km north of Guyamate, La Romana Province, Dominican Republic. Distribution: Hispaniola, Puerto Rico; the species has been recorded in the literature as C. longicollis.
